attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 4.2.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, Alpine 3.23) serving AMQP exclusively over TLS on port 5671, secured by a purpose-built CA. Client certificate authentication is mandatory (verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true); the plaintext 5672 listener is disabled entirely. The management UI (15672) is gated by an iptables chain (RMQ_MGMT) that only accepts traffic from the three cluster node IPs and drops everything else, persisted via rc-update/iptables-save. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified RabbitMQ/TLS/firewall/cluster membership fully recovered before moving to the next node, preserving quorum throughout. Along the way discovered and fixed a persistence bug: /etc/hostname was "localhost" (runtime hostname set out-of-band by provisioning), which caused node3's first reboot to rejoin the cluster under a spurious Erlang node name; fixed /etc/hostname on all three nodes and cleaned up the stray cluster member before node2/node1 restarts, after which both came back correctly as rabbit@node2/rabbit@node1.
